title: A transparent three-surrogate PPG respiratory-rate abstention rule did not beat raw PPG on held-out BIDMC records
abstract: In BIDMC v1.0.0 (53 eight-minute ICU recordings), we tested whether disagreement among three transparent PPG respiratory surrogates could select reliable 32-s respiratory-rate estimates. A fixed record-held-out design selected a 12.04 breaths/min disagreement threshold using 32 development records. On 21 untouched records, the selective median estimator retained 57.0% of valid windows but had record-mean MAE 4.08 breaths/min versus 2.49 for a raw-PPG spectral baseline (paired record bootstrap for baseline minus candidate: -2.91 to -0.39). Thus this simple agreement-based abstention rule did not improve accuracy, despite waveform-permutation falsification degrading both estimators. This is a scoped negative measurement result, not a clinical-performance claim.
